# Data Licensing and Scraping Ethics

This homework builds on the Considerations for Web Scraping lecture and Lab #4 by looking into data licensing and ethical considerations in web scraping.


## Background

Ownership of anything published on the world wide web is regulated by licenses. While sharing of materials and open access disseminates materials quickly, it does not mean that just because we can openly access something, it automatically belongs to us.

Most relevant to us are two sets of licenses: software licenses and data licenses. Dealing with licenses is often tricky because of all the legal language.

For our use, we want to answer some key questions:

* Do authors want to be cited for their work? (**Attribution**)
* Are the authors fine with others modifying their work and then sharing the modified work? (**Derivates**)
* Are the authors fine with other people making a profit from those derivations? (**Commercial use**)
* Who is responsible if the software does not do what it promises to do? (**Liability**)
* What can and cannot be used as part of the derivation process? (**AI use**)


Some references related to licensing:

* R Packages 2nd edition, [Chapter 12: Licensing](https://r-pkgs.org/license.html) by Hadley Wickham and Jennifer Bryan
* Research Outreach guide on [Creative Commons licensing](https://researchoutreach.org/articles/thought-leaders/license-to-share-how-the-creative-commons-licensing-system-encourages-the-remixing-and-reuse-of-published-materials/)
